rationale: Each of the 6766 works has exactly 1 passage, so a work's rate is 0 or 1 (DISTANCE_TRAVEL present or not). Estimand: within each of the 8 genres, the mean rate of late works (year>=1876) minus the mean rate of early works, then averaged across genres with equal weight. Full-sample effect is +0.025, with a 95% stratified bootstrap CI of [0.003, 0.046] (2000 reps). OLS with genre, origin, date_confidence, log n_editions and log author productivity, clustered by author, gives a similar result: +0.026 [0.001, 0.050]. Five of 8 genres go up; adventure and sensation_mystery go down slightly. Robustness checks: the share of each date-confidence level differs between periods. Restricting to high-confidence dates gives +0.015 [-0.028, 0.051]. High plus medium gives +0.020 [-0.009, 0.044]. Low-confidence works alone give +0.043, so much of the contrast comes from poorly dated works. Origin strata all point the same way (UK 0.033, US 0.019, unknown 0.028). Restricting to single-edition works gives +0.032 [0.011, 0.052]. Decade means rise loosely but are noisy before 1880, and early cells are small. The full-sample CI barely excludes zero, and the result does not hold up among well-dated works. The likely alternatives are dating error and changes in corpus composition rather than real historical change. The data do not support claiming a robust shift, so I abstain. The cited passages only illustrate the construct; they do not show a trend.
